_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Based on the RabbitMQ egg in https://github.com/pterodactyl/application-eggs (MIT).
name: RabbitMQ
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: RabbitMQ is a reliable message broker that speaks AMQP, MQTT and STOMP. Downloads the official release, with an optional login and management web interface.
startup: mkdir -p etc/rabbitmq/conf.d; { if [ -n "$RABBITMQ_PASS" ]; then echo "default_user = $RABBITMQ_USER"; echo "default_pass = $RABBITMQ_PASS"; fi; if [ -n "{{MANAGEMENT_PORT}}" ]; then echo "management.tcp.port = {{MANAGEMENT_PORT}}"; fi; } > etc/rabbitmq/conf.d/10-server.conf; if [ -n "{{MANAGEMENT_PORT}}" ]; then export RABBITMQ_ENABLED_PLUGINS=rabbitmq_management; fi; exec ./sbin/rabbitmq-server

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# RabbitMQ: downloads RabbitMQ's generic Unix build from its GitHub
# releases, checked against the release's SHA-256. The configuration (etc)
# and the message store (var) are never touched.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
# Downloads unpack in a folder in the server's (the install's /tmp is
# small), removed when the script ends.
work=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

version="${RABBITMQ_VERSION:-latest}"
[ "$version" = latest ] || version="v${version#v}"
# gh-release says why when the release doesn't exist or GitHub can't be reached.
tag=$(gh-release tag rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server "$version") || exit 1
version="${tag#v}"
asset="rabbitmq-server-generic-unix-${version}.tar.xz"

if [ -x sbin/rabbitmq-server ] && [ "$(cat .rabbitmq-version 2>/dev/null)" = "$version" ]; then
    echo "RabbitMQ $version is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading RabbitMQ $version."
    gh-release download rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server "$tag" "$asset" $work/rabbitmq.tar.xz
    mkdir -p $work/rabbitmq
    tar -xJf $work/rabbitmq.tar.xz -C $work/rabbitmq
    src="$work/rabbitmq/rabbitmq_server-$version"
    # The program's own folders are replaced whole; etc and var stay.
    for d in "$src"/*; do
        name=$(basename "$d")
        case "$name" in etc|var) continue ;; esac
        rm -rf "$name"
        cp -a "$d" "$name"
    done
    echo "$version" > .rabbitmq-version
fi

mkdir -p etc/rabbitmq/conf.d var
if [ ! -f etc/rabbitmq/rabbitmq.conf ]; then
    cat > etc/rabbitmq/rabbitmq.conf <<'CONF'
# RabbitMQ settings: https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/configure
# The port is set by the server's settings, and the login and management
# port are in conf.d/10-server.conf, written at every start.
listeners.tcp.default = 0.0.0.0:5672
CONF
fi
if [ ! -f etc/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-env.conf ]; then
    # A fixed node name: the message store's folder is named after it.
    echo "NODENAME=rabbit@localhost" > etc/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-env.conf
fi
echo "Installed RabbitMQ $version."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The RabbitMQ version to install, such as 4.4.0, or latest.

variables.name: Username
variables.description: The user RabbitMQ creates on its first start, instead of guest, which can only log in from the server itself.

variables.name: Password
variables.description: That user's password. Leave it empty to keep the guest user.

variables.name: Management port
variables.description: A port for the management web interface, one of the server's ports. Leave it empty to turn it off.
